description:
`jit validate --fix` re-validates even when it applied zero fixes, so a repository whose
issue files disagree with `.jit/index.json` cannot receive a false clean bill.

## Background

Discovered while executing the documented divergence recovery procedure. On a repository
whose `.jit/index.json` disagrees with the issue files on disk (for example after a merge
conflict in the index was resolved to one side), plain `jit validate` fails with exit 4
naming the disagreement, while `jit validate --fix` prints "No fixes needed" and exits 0:
`validate_with_fix` re-runs validation only when it applied at least one fix, so the
zero-fix path never observes the failure plain validation reports. `jit recover` does not
rebuild the issue index either (its index line concerns the claims index), and a later
ordinary mutation appends to the stale index rather than rebuilding it, so an issue record
present on disk stays invisible to listing and lookup indefinitely. The recovery guidance
routes around this by instructing manual union resolution verified with plain `jit
validate`; the command itself remains wrong.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `jit validate --fix` on a repository with a stale or one-sided `.jit/index.json` reports the disagreement (or repairs it) instead of exiting 0 with "No fixes needed"; its exit status never contradicts plain `jit validate` on the same repository state.
- [hard] REQ-02: Coverage reproduces the false-clean case (index/issue-file disagreement with zero other fixable findings) and fails if the zero-fix path stops re-validating.
- [hard] REQ-03: Whether index rebuilding becomes a `--fix` repair or stays a refusal with guidance is decided and documented where validate's behavior is documented.


Steward ruling 2026-10-21: duplicate of @/issue/9876a23a requirement REQ-14 (`validate --fix` always reports one report computed after the fixes, including when it applied none). Delivered there.
title: Re-validate after zero-fix jit validate --fix
